text:
Predicates:
Adores(x, y) ::: x adores y.
DesignStyle(x, y) ::: x is y style.
InterestingGeometries(x) ::: x has interesting geometries.
Brutalist(x) ::: x is a brutalist building.
ZahaHadid(x) ::: x is Zaha Hadid.
KellyWearstler(x) ::: x is Kelly Wearstler.
Evocative(x) ::: x is evocative.
Dreamy(x) ::: x is dreamy.
DesignBy(x, y) ::: x is a design by y.

Premises:
∀x (Adores(x, y) ∧ DesignStyle(y, z) → InterestingGeometries(y)) ::: All styles adored by Max have interesting geometries.
¬∃x (Adores(x, y) ∧ DesignStyle(y, brutalist)) ::: No adored style by Max is a brutalist style.
∀x (Adores(x, y) → (DesignStyle(y, z) ∨ DesignStyle(y, w))) ::: Every style Max adores is either Zaha Hadid's style or Kelly Wearstler's style.
∀x (DesignStyle(y, z) ∧ Adores(x, y) ∧ KellyWearstler(y) → Evocative(y)) ::: All Kelly Wearstler styles adored by Max are evocative.
∀x (DesignStyle(y, w) ∧ Adores(x, y) ∧ KellyWearstler(y) → Dreamy(y)) ::: All Kelly Wearstler styles adored by Max are dreamy.
∀x ((DesignBy(x, y) ∧ Adores(x, y) ∧ InterestingGeometries(y)) → (Brutalist(x) ∧ Evocative(x))) ::: If a design by Max that he adores has interesting geometries, then it is a brutalist building and evocative.

Conclusion:
A design by Max is a brutalist building.
